Scenarios.Scenario: Explorer cut/move paste fails because the destination already exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The paste command reads clipboard resources, deduplicates parent paths, stats each source and resolves a target, then awaits one bulk-edit submission. On rejection, the changed code formats the existing error once and posts a notification; cut-state clipboard cleanup runs in finally. The formatting is after the filesystem failure and adds no new blocking boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the custom file-list clipboard buffer through the native host on desktop; the web implementation performs one browser clipboard read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clipboard read per paste invocation when no native FileList is supplied, independent of N resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one clipboard read occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before pasted resources can be resolved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat each deduplicated source resource and, when overwrite naming is disabled, check whether each candidate destination exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N source stat calls in parallel after deduplication; up to N destination-existence checks depending on naming mode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-resource checks and Promise.all scheduling occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All source checks and any overwrite checks complete before bulk edit submission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply the move as one bulk-edit service submission containing the resolved ResourceFileEdit entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bulk-edit submission per paste, containing up to N edits and underlying filesystem work proportional to N; this scenario rejects on the conflicting edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bulk edit and filesystem work occurred before the diff; only the eventual error text wrapping changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The operation is awaited and its rejection leads to the changed notification-formatting line.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write or clear resource clipboard state through setToCopy during cut setup and finally cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write for the prior cut; on failure cleanup calls writeResources once with an empty list (desktop short-circuits without native-host IPC, while web updates the browser clipboard).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cut setup and finally cleanup were identical before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial cut must finish before paste; failure cleanup is awaited before pasteFileHandler resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct top-level clipboard resources after distinctParents; source stat/target resolution and the bulk edit scale with N. The changed formatter executes once per failed paste command, not once per resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source stat and target-resolution tasks run concurrently through Promise.all across the N deduplicated resources. A single bulk-edit call containing all edits is then awaited. Error formatting and notification are serialized once after rejection; no new concurrency or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Desktop clipboard resources are read and parsed on each paste; web uses the custom clipboard MIME type with an in-memory/state-hash fallback. There is no error-formatting cache, but the formatter runs only once per failed command. The diff does not change cold/warm behavior, keys, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk is reached exactly once in the catch block after a failed operation, and formatter implementations show no added boundary, retention, or repeated per-resource work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem/provider latency and the number of selected resources vary, but all scaling work is pre-existing. The changed failure formatter replaces localized wrapping plus an Error allocation with one direct conversion, so there is no plausible added performance magnitude.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes localization/string wrapping and an intermediate Error allocation while preserving a single synchronous formatting call after failure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explorer copy/paste or native file paste succeeds
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Clipboard/native FileList acquisition, optional confirmation, parallel source validation, one bulk copy edit, explorer selection, and possible single-editor open must complete. The changed catch line is not reached, so it is off this scenario's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read clipboard resources when the command is not supplied a native FileList.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per paste invocation; omitted when a FileList is provided.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat path sources, optionally check destination existence, read native File contents, and apply copy edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Validation/read work scales with N resources and total file bytes; one bulk-edit submission contains all accepted edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical before the diff; the modified catch block is never executed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations form the successful paste critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct top-level paths or native files; validation and content reads scale with N, and file byte allocation scales with total pasted content size. None of this work is changed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-file validation and native File.arrayBuffer creation are initiated through Promise.all; edits are coalesced into one awaited bulk-edit call. The diff does not alter concurrency, limiting, or ordering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Clipboard behavior is the same desktop per-read parsing or web custom-MIME/in-memory fallback. No cache or coalescing behavior changes on successful paste.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: control flow bypasses the catch block on success, and the import removal has no runtime effect.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and file-size costs vary, but no changed instruction executes on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression because successful paste behavior, boundary count, allocation scale, cache behavior, and concurrency are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. The production hunk only simplifies one failure-path error conversion; it adds no boundary call, repeated work, retention, eager initialization, or concurrency, and the added test does not affect product runtime.
